In a method and an associated brewing apparatus for preparing a hot beverage, in particular a coffee beverage, a quantity of a flavoring source, in particular coffee powder, is introduced into a brewing chamber and then, in a brewing operation, a predeterminable overall quantity of brewing water is passed through the brewing chamber under pressure, in order to enhance the taste quality of the freshly brewed coffee beverages or at least to increase the consistency of the taste. outputs.L3:
A method and brewing apparatus are provided for preparing hot beverages, in particular freshly brewed coffee. In this process, a portion of coffee powder is introduced into a brewing chamber, where it is contacted with hot brewing water. During the brewing operation, a predetermined total quantity of brewing water is conveyed through the brewing chamber under pressure, so that the water extracts aroma and flavor substances from the coffee powder before the finished beverage is dispensed.

The method is designed to improve the taste quality of the brewed coffee and/or to increase the reproducibility and consistency of the taste from one brewing operation to the next. To achieve this, the brewing process is not controlled solely by fixed preset parameters. Instead, during the brewing operation, the system repeatedly or continuously determines relevant process values. These values may include the instantaneous flow rate of the brewing water, the quantity of water that has already passed through the brewing chamber, and/or the quantity of brewing water that still remains to be delivered.

Based on these measured or calculated values, the pressure conditions in the brewing system are actively regulated. For this purpose, a controllable motor-operated needle backpressure valve is arranged downstream of the brewing chamber. The valve can be adjusted with precision during the brewing process in order to vary the backpressure acting on the brewing chamber.

A controller receives the measured values relating to water flow and/or water quantity and uses them to control the position of the needle backpressure valve. By opening or closing the valve to a defined extent, the controller can influence the pressure and flow behavior of the brewing water as it passes through the coffee powder. In this way, the extraction process can be adapted dynamically during brewing, helping to compensate for variations such as differences in coffee grind size, powder quantity, tamping density, or other brewing conditions.

As a result, the apparatus and method allow the brewing process to be controlled more accurately. This can lead to improved flavor development, better extraction of desirable coffee components, and a more uniform beverage quality across repeated preparations.
outputs.L4:
A hot-beverage brewing method and corresponding apparatus are provided for preparing coffee or similar brewed beverages with improved and more reproducible taste quality. In the method, a predetermined quantity of brewing water is heated and supplied under pressure to a brewing chamber that contains a portion of coffee powder. The brewing water is forced through the coffee powder so that soluble flavoring substances, oils, and aromatic compounds are extracted and delivered as a finished beverage.

During the brewing operation, at least one brewing parameter associated with the amount of water flowing through the coffee powder is monitored. This may include, for example, the actual flow rate of the brewing water, the total quantity of water already delivered, the elapsed brewing time, or a combination of these values. The measured values are supplied to a controller, which compares them with stored target values or desired brewing profiles. In this way, the system can determine whether the extraction process is proceeding too quickly, too slowly, or in accordance with the intended brewing conditions.

To influence the extraction process, the apparatus includes a backpressure valve arranged downstream of the brewing chamber. The backpressure valve is preferably formed as a motor-operated needle valve, the opening cross-section of which can be precisely adjusted by the controller. By changing the position of the needle valve, the controller varies the flow resistance downstream of the coffee powder and thereby regulates the pressure conditions in the brewing chamber. If the measured flow rate is too high, the controller can reduce the valve opening to increase backpressure and slow the flow. If the flow rate is too low, the controller can open the valve further to reduce backpressure and permit a greater flow of beverage.

This controlled adjustment of the downstream backpressure makes it possible to compensate for variations in the coffee powder, such as differences in grind size, tamping pressure, quantity, freshness, or degree of swelling during extraction. As a result, the brewing water can be guided through the coffee bed under more stable and repeatable conditions. The desired amount of water can be passed through the coffee powder within a defined time range and under a controlled pressure profile, which leads to a more consistent extraction.

The apparatus may include a water reservoir or water connection, a pump for supplying pressurized water, a heater or boiler for bringing the water to the desired brewing temperature, the brewing chamber for receiving the coffee powder, one or more sensors for detecting flow rate or water quantity, the motor-operated needle backpressure valve, and an electronic controller. The controller may store brewing programs for different beverage types and may operate the pump, heater, and valve in coordination with one another. The sensor signals allow the controller to continuously or periodically adjust the valve position during the brewing cycle.

By actively controlling the downstream resistance rather than relying only on a fixed outlet restriction or the random resistance of the coffee powder itself, the method provides more uniform brewing conditions from one beverage preparation to the next. This can reduce undesirable taste variations caused by under-extraction or over-extraction. The resulting beverage can therefore have a more stable flavor, improved aroma, better crema formation in the case of espresso, and overall higher quality.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention relating to a coffee machine brewing method that monitors water flow/quantity during brewing and controls a motorized needle backpressure valve downstream of the brewing chamber.
counterfactuals.output: A coffee machine brewing method is disclosed in which water is delivered through a brewing chamber containing coffee material while a flow parameter representative of water flow rate and/or delivered water quantity is monitored during extraction. A control unit receives measurement signals from a flow sensor and regulates a motorized needle backpressure valve arranged downstream of the brewing chamber in a beverage outlet path. During brewing, the control unit adjusts the position of the needle valve to vary hydraulic resistance downstream of the brewing chamber, thereby controlling extraction pressure, flow rate, or a pressure-flow profile as a function of the monitored water flow or quantity. The valve may be progressively opened or closed according to predetermined brewing phases, target cumulative volumes, detected flow deviations, or feedback control logic, to compensate for variations in coffee dose, grind size, tamping, or capsule permeability. The method enables repeatable beverage volume, improved extraction consistency, and dynamic control of crema and flavor characteristics without requiring manual adjustment of backpressure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of a brewing apparatus for preparing hot coffee beverages, where coffee powder is placed in a brewing chamber, pressurized water passes through it, and a controller adjusts a downstream backpressure valve based on measured flow or volume.
counterfactuals.output: A brewing apparatus for hot coffee beverages includes a brewing chamber configured to hold coffee powder and receive pressurized hot water to extract coffee. Downstream of the brewing chamber, an adjustable backpressure valve regulates the outlet resistance and thus the extraction pressure and flow behavior. A flow or volume sensor measures the amount or rate of beverage discharged from the brewing chamber. A controller receives the measured flow/volume data and actuates the backpressure valve accordingly, for example to maintain a target flow profile, extraction pressure, or dispensed beverage volume. This closed-loop control enables consistent extraction conditions and improved repeatability of coffee quality.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract in European patent language for a method and apparatus that improves coffee taste consistency by continuously determining brewing water flow upstream/downstream of the brewing chamber and activating a motor-operated needle valve accordingly.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a method and an apparatus for preparing coffee beverages, in particular in an automatic coffee machine, wherein brewing water is supplied to a brewing chamber containing coffee material. In order to improve taste consistency, a flow of the brewing water is continuously determined at a measuring location upstream and/or downstream of the brewing chamber during a brewing operation. A control unit compares the determined flow with a predetermined target flow profile and actuates a motor-operated needle valve arranged in the water path in dependence on the comparison. By adjusting an opening cross-section of the needle valve during extraction, deviations caused by variations in coffee quantity, grinding degree, tamping pressure, ageing of the coffee material or hydraulic tolerances are compensated. The apparatus comprises at least one flow sensor, the motor-operated needle valve, the brewing chamber and the control unit configured to carry out the method. A substantially reproducible extraction profile and thus improved consistency of coffee taste are thereby obtained.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a coffee brewing invention in formal patent wording: during extraction, measure the volume flow or remaining/passed brewing water quantity and use that value to control a motor-driven needle valve positioned after the brewing chamber.
counterfactuals.output:
A coffee brewing apparatus and method are disclosed for regulating extraction of a coffee beverage. The apparatus comprises a brewing chamber configured to receive ground coffee and brewing water, a discharge conduit arranged downstream of the brewing chamber, a motor-actuated needle valve disposed in the discharge conduit, and at least one measuring device configured to determine, during an extraction process, a volume flow of the beverage or brewing water, a quantity of brewing water already passed through the brewing chamber, and/or a quantity of brewing water remaining to be passed through the brewing chamber. A control unit is operatively connected to the measuring device and to a drive motor of the needle valve.

During extraction, the control unit receives a measured value representative of the volume flow and/or the passed or remaining brewing water quantity and, in dependence on said measured value, actuates the drive motor to adjust the position of the needle valve. The needle valve thereby varies the flow resistance downstream of the brewing chamber so as to influence the pressure and flow conditions prevailing in the brewing chamber during extraction. In this manner, the extraction profile may be controlled as a function of extraction progress, for example by reducing or increasing the outflow cross-section of the needle valve in accordance with a predetermined control curve, target flow rate, target pressure, or target extraction time.

In one embodiment, the control unit compares the measured passed water quantity or remaining water quantity with a stored extraction profile and controls the motor-driven needle valve such that different valve positions are assumed at different stages of the extraction. In another embodiment, the measured instantaneous volume flow is used in a closed-loop control system to maintain a desired flow rate through the coffee puck. The needle valve is preferably arranged after the brewing chamber in the direction of flow, such that regulation is effected on the outlet side of the brewing chamber. The motor drive may comprise a stepper motor, servo motor, or other electrically controllable actuator enabling reproducible positioning of the needle valve.

**Exemplary patent claim wording**

1. A coffee brewing apparatus comprising:  
   a brewing chamber configured to contain coffee material and to receive brewing water during an extraction operation;  
   an outlet line arranged downstream of the brewing chamber;  
   a needle valve arranged in the outlet line downstream of the brewing chamber;  
   an electric motor configured to adjust a position of the needle valve;  
   a measuring device configured to determine, during the extraction operation, at least one value selected from a volume flow, a quantity of brewing water passed through the brewing chamber, and a quantity of brewing water remaining for the extraction operation; and  
   a control unit connected to the measuring device and to the electric motor,  
   wherein the control unit is configured to control the electric motor, during the extraction operation, as a function of the determined value so as to adjust the needle valve and thereby regulate an outflow from the brewing chamber.

2. The coffee brewing apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the control unit is configured to adjust the needle valve in accordance with a predetermined extraction profile dependent on the quantity of brewing water already passed through the brewing chamber.

3. The coffee brewing apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the control unit is configured to adjust the needle valve in accordance with a predetermined extraction profile dependent on the quantity of brewing water remaining to be supplied or passed during the extraction operation.

4. The coffee brewing apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the measuring device comprises a flow meter arranged upstream of the brewing chamber, downstream of the brewing chamber, or in a water supply line leading to the brewing chamber.

5. The coffee brewing apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the control unit is configured to perform closed-loop control of the needle valve to maintain a target volume flow during at least a portion of the extraction operation.

6. The coffee brewing apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the electric motor is a stepper motor configured to move the needle valve into defined valve positions.

7. A method for brewing coffee, comprising:  
   supplying brewing water to a brewing chamber containing coffee material;  
   extracting coffee beverage from the brewing chamber through an outlet line;  
   measuring, during extraction, at least one of a volume flow, a quantity of brewing water passed through the brewing chamber, and a quantity of brewing water remaining for extraction; and  
   controlling, as a function of the measured value, an electric motor coupled to a needle valve arranged downstream of the brewing chamber, thereby adjusting the needle valve during extraction to regulate the outflow from the brewing chamber.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a patent abstract for a hot beverage preparation system with a brewing chamber, pressure-driven water supply, flow/quantity sensing during brewing, and a controllable downstream backpressure valve opened or closed by a drive motor.
counterfactuals.output: A hot beverage preparation system comprises a brewing chamber configured to receive a beverage precursor, a pressure-driven water supply arranged to deliver heated water through the brewing chamber during a brewing operation, and at least one sensor configured to detect a flow rate and/or delivered quantity of water during the brewing operation. Downstream of the brewing chamber, a controllable backpressure valve is arranged in a beverage outlet path to selectively restrict or release beverage flow from the brewing chamber. The backpressure valve is operatively coupled to a drive motor configured to open and close the valve in response to a control signal. A controller receives signals from the sensor and controls the drive motor to adjust the state of the backpressure valve based on detected flow and/or quantity parameters, thereby regulating extraction pressure, beverage discharge, or brewing completion. The system enables controlled pressure buildup and release during preparation of coffee, espresso, or other hot beverages.
